actual_answer: If you received an unexpected MFA prompt after your phone was stolen, you must contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow]. The Help Desk will verify your identity, revoke the old authenticator registration, and begin device re-enrolment [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow]. Security escalation is mandatory if you report an unexpected MFA prompt [SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices].

Advise the employee to report suspected compromise to Security Operations. Because an unexpected MFA prompt was reported, Security escalation is mandatory and the case also receives the Security Review classification.

question: What information must the Help Desk record in an MFA recovery ticket?
actual_answer: To record in an MFA recovery ticket, you must include [OPS-09::required-ticket-fields] the following: employee identifier, corporate contact channel, affected payroll function, deadline if any, device-loss status, verification methods attempted, verification outcome, old-authenticator revocation status, re-enrolment outcome, retrieved policy version, and every escalation made. [OPS-09::employee-communication] You must also inform the employee of the recovery stage progress, their next action, and that the enrolment link expires after 30 minutes. Finally, [OPS-09::closure-evidence] you should close the ticket only after recording the old registration as revoked, the new device as enrolled, and a successful test sign-in.
